raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A `/generate` request with `"priority": 9223372036854775807` (INT64_MAX) terminates the scheduler once the request finishes. When a finished request's KV is cached, the radix cache re-inserts the prompt one priority above the request so that eviction drops the output KV before the prompt. With the Rust tree core (the default), `InsertParams.priority` is an `i64`, so the re-insert at `priority + 1` raises `OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C long` inside the scheduler loop. The legacy Python cache does not crash but stores a value outside the signed 64-bit range.

Nothing validates the request priority on the way in, so a client (or a misconfigured default priority) can bring the engine down with one request.

## Modifications

- `RadixCache` and `UnifiedRadixCache`: the prompt priority boost is `min(priority + 1, INT64_MAX)`. The request's own priority is unchanged; only the boosted prompt copy saturates.
- `TokenizerManager._set_default_priority`: after applying the configured default, a priority outside `[-2**63, 2**63 - 1]` raises `ValueError` before `_init_req_state`, so the request is rejected at the API layer instead of failing inside the scheduler. The check applies whether or not priority scheduling is enabled, since the priority still reaches the cache either way.

Tests (each fails on the pre-fix code and passes with it):

- `test_rust_tree_core_integration.py`: a real CPU `UnifiedRadixCache` on the Rust core releases a finished request at `INT64_MAX - 1` and `INT64_MAX`; the recorded insert priorities are `[priority, INT64_MAX]` (no overflow, no over-clamp) and the full sequence is still matchable.
- `test_radix_cache_unit.py`: the existing prompt/output split fixture is shared with a new case asserting both nodes hold `INT64_MAX` after a request at `INT64_MAX`.
- `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py`: the INT64 boundary values pass through `_set_default_priority` unchanged; `INT64_MIN - 1` and `INT64_MAX + 1` from the body or from the configured default raise `ValueError` from `generate_request` before `_init_req_state` is called, with priority scheduling on and off.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model forward code or kernels.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one `min()` per finished request and one range comparison per incoming request.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

+class TestPriorityRange(CustomTestCase):
+    """Request priorities reach the radix cache as signed 64-bit integers, so an
+    out-of-range value is rejected before dispatch instead of failing inside
+    the scheduler, and the boundary values themselves pass through unchanged."""
+
+    INT64_MIN = -(1 << 63)
+    INT64_MAX = (1 << 63) - 1
+
+    def test_int64_boundaries_are_preserved(self):
+        tm = _make_tokenizer_manager(self)
+        tm.enable_priority_scheduling = True
+        tm.default_priority_value = 0
+        for priority in (self.INT64_MIN, self.INT64_MAX):
+            with self.subTest(priority=priority):
+                obj = GenerateReqInput(input_ids=[1], priority=priority)
+                tm._set_default_priority(obj)
+                self.assertEqual(obj.priority, priority)
+
+    def test_out_of_range_priority_is_rejected_before_dispatch(self):
+        for enabled in (False, True):
+            for priority in (self.INT64_MIN - 1, self.INT64_MAX + 1):
+                for source in ("body", "default"):
+                    if source == "default" and not enabled:
+                        continue
+                    with self.subTest(
+                        enabled=enabled, priority=priority, source=source
+                    ):
+                        tm = _make_tm_for_generate(self)
+                        del tm._set_default_priority  # the real one is under test
+                        tm.enable_priority_scheduling = enabled
+                        tm.default_priority_value = (
+                            priority if source == "default" else 0
+                        )
+                        tm._init_req_state = Mock()
+                        obj = GenerateReqInput(
+                            input_ids=[1],
+                            priority=priority if source == "body" else None,
+                        )
+                        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "signed 64-bit"):
+                            asyncio.run(tm.generate_request(obj).__anext__())
+                        tm._init_req_state.assert_not_called()
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":

+# ---- request priority at the i64 boundary ----
+
+
+class _RecordingUnifiedRadixCache(UnifiedRadixCache):
+    def __init__(self, params):
+        self.insert_priorities = []
+        super().__init__(params)
+
+    def insert(self, params):
+        self.insert_priorities.append(params.priority)
+        return super().insert(params)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("priority", [(1 << 63) - 2, (1 << 63) - 1])
+def test_finished_request_prompt_priority_saturates_at_int64_max(priority):
+    """Caching a finished request re-inserts its prompt one priority above the
+    request so eviction drops the output first. The core stores priority as a
+    signed 64-bit integer, so the boost must saturate at INT64_MAX instead of
+    overflowing the binding and failing the insert."""
+    from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs, set_global_server_args_for_scheduler
+
+    # release_kv_cache reads the serving config off the published bags.
+    set_global_server_args_for_scheduler(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy"))
+    req_to_token_pool = ReqToTokenPool(
+        size=2, max_context_len=16, device="cpu", enable_memory_saver=False
+    )
+    allocator = TokenToKVPoolAllocator(
+        size=16, dtype=torch.float32, device="cpu", kvcache=None, need_sort=False
+    )
+    cache = _RecordingUnifiedRadixCache(
+        CacheInitParams(
+            disable=False,
+            req_to_token_pool=req_to_token_pool,
+            token_to_kv_pool_allocator=allocator,
+            page_size=1,
+            tree_components=(ComponentType.FULL,),
+            tree_core_backend="rust",
+        )
+    )
+    req = Req(
+        rid="priority",
+        origin_input_text=None,
+        origin_input_ids=array("q", [1, 2, 3]),
+        sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_new_tokens=2),
+        priority=priority,
+    )
+    req.output_ids = array("q", [4, 5])
+    req.finished_reason = "finished"
+    (req.kv.req_pool_idx,) = req_to_token_pool.alloc([req])
+    req.lock = cache.lock(cache.root_node_handle())
+    indices = allocator.alloc(5)
+    assert indices is not None
+    req_to_token_pool.write((req.kv.req_pool_idx, slice(0, 5)), indices)
+    req.kv.kv_committed_len = req.kv.kv_allocated_len = 5
+
+    release_kv_cache(req, cache, checkpoint=True)
+
+    assert req.priority == priority
+    assert cache.insert_priorities == [priority, (1 << 63) - 1]
+    match = cache.match_prefix(
+        MatchPrefixParams(key=RadixKey(req.origin_input_ids + req.output_ids))
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(cache.path_device_indices(match.last_device_node), indices)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))
